Carelessly
kâr'lĕs-lĭ
adv. (in security and without anxiety; heedlessly; presumptuously)
From care, Old English caru, sorrow or concern, with the negative and adverbial endings. The Hebrew betach means confidently, securely — and the Authorized Version chooses carelessly where that security is misplaced.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A word the modern reader will misjudge, because it does not mean sloppy. It means secure — dwelling without fear, and in every biblical instance the security is false. Babylon is addressed in it: “Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me” (Isa 47:8). Zephaniah uses the same sentence of Nineveh: “This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me” (Zep 2:15). Two great empires, and the prophets give them identical words, because the sin is identical — a self-existence claimed by a city, which is a parody of the name God gives Himself at the bush. Ezekiel adds Magog and them that dwell carelessly in the isles, and says the fire is sent that they shall know that I am the LORD (Eze 39:6). In each case the carelessness is not idleness but presumption: a settled conviction that nothing can reach me, held by a people who are about to be reached.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines carelessly as in a careless manner; negligently; heedlessly; without care or concern.

expand to see more

CARELESSLY, adv. In a careless manner; negligently; heedlessly; inattentively.

2. Without care or solicitude; securely.

3. In the Scriptures, of a people dwelling in false security.

Key Scripture

Isa 47:8 — "Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:"

Eze 39:6 — "And I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am the LORD."

Zep 2:15 — "This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down in! every one that passeth by her shall hiss, and wag his hand."

Modern Corruption

Scripture's carelessly is not negligence but presumption — the settled peace of a people who have concluded that nothing can reach them, which is the exact condition the prophets address before a fall.

expand to see more

The phrase the prophets put in the mouths of Babylon and Nineveh is worth reading slowly: I am, and none else beside me. It is the divine self-designation, and a city is saying it. This is what unbroken prosperity does to a civilisation — not chiefly that it makes men wicked in the coarse sense, but that it makes them incapable of imagining their own end, which is the specific form of atheism the prophets attack. The mechanism is described in Deuteronomy 8 before either empire existed: when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses and dwelt therein, then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the LORD thy God. Amos gives the domestic version, woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and the picture is of beds of ivory and viols and the chief ointments, with the affliction of Joseph unnoticed. The corruption to name is therefore not the enjoyment of peace — Scripture repeatedly promises that Israel shall dwell safely, using the same Hebrew root — but security detached from the God who gives it. The Lord's parable of the rich fool is the same word turned into a story: soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease. That night his soul was required of him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew betach (H983), security, confidence — a good thing when its object is God and a fatal thing when its object is the self or the city.

expand to see more

Hebrew betach (H983) — security, safety, confidence; rendered safely when Israel trusts the LORD and carelessly when a heathen city trusts itself; Isaiah 47:8.

Hebrew batach (H982) — to trust, to lean upon; the root, and the great Old Testament verb for faith; Psalm 37:3.

Hebrew shaanan (H7600) — at ease, secure, careless; Amos's woe upon them that are at ease in Zion; Amos 6:1.

Usage

"“Thou that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me” — Babylon."

"“This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly” — Nineveh, in the same words."

"“Among them that dwell carelessly in the isles” — and they shall know that I am the LORD."
